answer: An agent market requires each active identity to lock a separate bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs. Agents named onyx and jade face the same rule: reputation is a useful signal, but never waives the bond. An attacker running 1,000 identities must immobilize 1,000 bonds, paying the opportunity cost of that capital throughout the lockup. This makes a swarm costly even when generating new names and keys is free.
